findings.title: Mutex contention hotspot at 0x000000262376f070
findings.summary: 1 threads waited 40 times (10/s) for mutex 0x000000262376f070; someone was waiting 3% of the time; p99 wait 3.33 ms.
findings.qnx_note: Every MUTEX-state interval is real contention: uncontended QNX mutexes never enter the kernel. Shrink the critical section (copy outside the lock), split the lock per resource, or hand buffers between threads with message passing.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in bm_low
findings.summary: bm_low (prio 10) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 80 of its 100 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 80 ms. It stands out in: longest wait for a CPU (higher than healthy), time waiting for a CPU (higher than healthy), time asleep (lower than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is healthy_irq_deferred (distance 0.07, inside the 0.852 typical for that pattern).
findings.qnx_note: Learned from healthy QNX 8.0 traces: this thread behaved unlike any healthy run in the features listed. It is not a proven bug and gets no automatic fix: look at the timeline around it. Any resemblance to a known pattern is measured against labelled example windows, never a rule that fired.

findings.title: Unusual behaviour in bm_high
findings.summary: bm_high (prio 30) behaved unlike healthy QNX programs in 40 of its 61 time windows; the most unusual stretch lasted 20 ms. It stands out in: time blocked on a mutex (higher than healthy), longest single block (higher than healthy), longest unbroken time holding a CPU (lower than healthy). The closest pattern TraceLens has seen is healthy mixed workload (periodic work, a mutex and message passing), but only loosely (distance 1.12 against 0.698 typical for it): treat this as behaviour of its own.
